front: What is the law of demand?
back: As price rises, quantity demanded falls, holding all else equal — this is why the demand curve slopes downward.
The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so the market clears with no surplus or shortage.
Price set above equilibrium, so quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

front: Name two things that shift the demand curve to the right.
back: Rising consumer income (for normal goods), or a rise in the price of a substitute good.

front: What does it mean if demand is 'elastic'?
back: Quantity demanded changes by a larger percentage than price does — buyers are highly sensitive to price changes.
